gaps.construct: Fun parameter: an ordering function passed as a value and called as Fun(H1, H2)
gaps.description: The doc has no type for an operation held in a parameter and no syntax to call one. Invented `an Operation from T and T to Bool` and `apply fun to h1 and h2`.

gaps.construct: Effects and failures of the passed Fun
gaps.description: uses/fails with lines are fixed per operation; there is no way to say the operation's effects are those of its function argument (effect polymorphism). Translation assumes Fun is pure.

gaps.construct: Boolean result type of Fun (true/false clauses)
gaps.description: The doc never names a boolean type or the literals true/false; invented `Bool`.
`T` appears only inside `type Queue of T`; the doc does not say how an operation declares a type parameter. Used T as if in scope.

gaps.construct: Multi-clause function head matching [H2 | T2] versus []
gaps.description: choose only matches choices and maybe values; clause selection rewritten as `if l2 is empty` followed by the cons case.

gaps.construct: Head/tail destructuring of a cons list
gaps.description: No head/tail pattern or tail operation. Tail rebuilt with a comprehension over indices, which copies the list and changes complexity from O(n) to O(n^2) per merge.

gaps.construct: Implicit allocation of cons cells on a GC heap
gaps.description: Doc example 21 requires an explicit Allocator and `uses memory` for any allocating operation, so an allocator is threaded through all recursive calls and OutOfMemory becomes a declared failure; list literals and `followed by` inside expressions have no place to name the allocator.
The doc has no recursion example; it does not say whether recursive operations need `decreases` or whether a call in `give back` position is a tail call.

Bare juxtaposition `ufmerge2_2 h1 t1 fun t2 m` is ambiguous (`fun t2` reads as a call), so label words were invented per operation; the doc does not say how operations with many unlabelled arguments are written.

doc_rules_contradicted: "Every operation that allocates must say so in `uses`, and the allocator is a value passed in. There is no hidden allocation" - the list literal `[h1]`, `followed by` and the tail comprehension allocate inside expressions with no allocator named
invented_syntax: an Operation from T and T to Bool
apply fun to h1 and h2
`followed by` used in a code expression (doc shows it only in ensure lines)
label words `then`, `by`, `against`, `onto`, `after` in the operation headers
notes: Higher-order functions are the core of this function and Scribe has neither function types nor a way to propagate a callback's effects into the caller's header. Cons-list idioms (head/tail match, O(1) prepend, reverse-onto) have no direct vocabulary, and the obvious index-based rewrite silently changes complexity.
